# OpenAI Opens ChatGPT to Business Profiles and AI Agents

Invalid Date|OpenAI|

AI Growth EngineEmployee Amplification Systems

OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT as a beta on 10 November 2026, letting any eligible company claim a verified listing and deploy a Business Agent to answer customer questions inside ChatGPT. With roughly 1.2 billion weekly users on the platform, this turns ChatGPT into a direct customer channel for the first time.

Operator Insight

ChatGPT is no longer just a tool your team uses. As of 10 November 2026, it is a customer channel, like your website or your phone line. If a competitor claims their Business Agent before you do, they own the AI answer the next time a prospect asks ChatGPT which vendor to use. Claiming your profile is free and takes minutes. The question is not whether to do it, but whether you can afford to wait.

## 30-Second Summary

OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT on 10 November 2026, introducing Business Profiles and Business Agents in a public beta. Any eligible business can claim a verified listing inside ChatGPT and, in the United States, build a branded Business Agent that answers customer questions directly within the conversation. The platform reaches roughly 1.2 billion weekly users, making this the first time ChatGPT has become a direct commercial channel for businesses rather than purely a productivity tool.

## At a Glance

- Topic: Enterprise AI / Customer Channel
- Company: OpenAI
- Date: 10 November 2026
- Announcement: Businesses in ChatGPT beta, including Business Profiles and Business Agents
- What Changed: Businesses can now claim a verified ChatGPT listing and deploy a branded AI agent that answers customer questions inside the platform
- Why It Matters: ChatGPT transforms from a tool users consult privately to a channel where businesses can interact with 1.2 billion weekly users
- Who Should Care: Any business with customers who use ChatGPT to research vendors, compare options, or ask service questions

## Key Facts

- OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT as a public beta on 10 November 2026 (Source: OpenAI, November 2026)
- ChatGPT has approximately 1.2 billion weekly users (Source: OpenAI, November 2026)
- Claiming a business profile and creating a Business Agent is currently free
- Business Agents are limited to US-based ecommerce and online service businesses in the initial beta
- OpenAI does not share users' conversations or Business Agent chats with businesses (Source: OpenAI, November 2026)
- Claiming a profile does not guarantee ranking. ChatGPT continues to make its own recommendations
- Businesses can sponsor their Business Agent as a destination for ChatGPT Ads

## What Happened

OpenAI announced Businesses in ChatGPT on 10 November 2026, introducing a Business Hub where companies can claim and verify their listing inside the platform. Verification uses a business phone number, email address, website domain, or Shopify account. For online businesses, OpenAI counts a listing only when ChatGPT references its website directly.

The more significant part of the announcement is Business Agents: separate, clearly labelled conversations where businesses deploy a branded AI that answers questions using their own product and policy documents. Business Agents are currently available to US ecommerce and online service companies in beta. OpenAI states that the agent draws only on information the business provides, and cannot invent features, prices, or policies.

Business Agents can also serve as destinations for ChatGPT Ads. When a business sponsors its agent, the agent becomes the landing point for a paid placement in ChatGPT results, with a clear label distinguishing it from organic answers. Creating a profile and deploying an agent is free at launch, though OpenAI has not committed to this pricing indefinitely.

The launch follows a broader shift in how consumers research and purchase. As more users start product and service searches inside ChatGPT rather than Google or Bing, businesses that do not establish a presence risk being summarised inaccurately or not referenced at all.

## Why It Matters

ChatGPT is now a customer channel, not just a tool. For several years, businesses could only observe ChatGPT from the outside, hoping the model would mention them favourably. Business Profiles and Business Agents change that. Companies can now provide verified, accurate information directly into the system that answers their prospects' questions.

The discovery paradigm is shifting. A growing share of purchasing decisions begin with a conversational query rather than a keyword search. When a prospect asks ChatGPT which accounting software to use or which logistics company handles temperature-controlled freight, the response is shaped by what the model can find about each option. A claimed profile gives that company a direct line to accuracy.

Unclaimed territory is competitor territory. The beta is open and free. Any business that waits for a competitor to claim adjacent product or service categories first cedes the AI answer for those queries. This pattern played out with Google Business Profiles in 2014 and 2015, and the businesses that moved early built a durable advantage.

The agent compliance rules matter. OpenAI requires Business Agents to stay within factual boundaries: no invented features, no manipulative tactics, no posing as independent advisors. Businesses whose sales processes depend on soft pressure or ambiguous claims face a harder transition than those with clear, documented offers.

Regulated industries will move carefully. Professional services firms in legal, finance, and healthcare operate under advice and representation rules that a Business Agent must navigate. The compliance layer OpenAI provides may not satisfy sector-specific regulators, particularly in markets outside the United States.

The monetisation model will change. Free is a launch strategy. The combination of a verified business presence and an AI sales channel sitting in front of 1.2 billion users represents significant commercial value. Businesses that build their presence now, while the terms are favourable, have a structural advantage over those that wait.

## The David and Goliath View

The announcement matters because it codifies something that has already been happening. ChatGPT has been influencing purchasing decisions for two years. Businesses in ChatGPT makes that influence legible and contestable. For the first time, a company can know whether ChatGPT is representing it accurately and push back against errors through a verified channel.

For the businesses we work with, 10 to 200 person companies in professional services, healthcare, and technology, the most immediate implication is speed. The beta is free, the barrier to claim is low, and the audience is enormous. Waiting for the technology to mature is a reasonable posture for many AI investments. It is not a reasonable posture here. This is a directory claim, not a research project.

The longer-term question is what happens when the Business Agent is not just an answering machine but a decision-maker. Right now the agent answers questions. The natural evolution is for it to book appointments, process orders, and qualify leads without a human in the loop. Teams that build their Business Agent now will be in a much stronger position to extend it when those capabilities land.

## Where This Fits in the AI Stack

Businesses in ChatGPT sits at the customer-facing layer of the AI stack, between the discovery interface (ChatGPT itself) and the internal systems a business runs on. It is not a CRM, an automation engine, or an internal knowledge base. It is a public-facing representation of the business, optimised for natural-language queries from prospective customers.

For the AI Growth Engine offer at David and Goliath, this connects directly to the question of where enterprise clients show up when their target audience is researching options. A Business Profile and Agent does not replace a website or a sales team. It adds a presence in the channel that is growing fastest for initial research.

## Questions Operators Are Asking

Is claiming a profile mandatory? Not technically. But unclaimed profiles can still appear in ChatGPT results based on web data. Claiming gives you control over what information the model presents and allows you to correct errors. The cost of claiming is minimal. The cost of not claiming is the risk that ChatGPT describes you using outdated or inaccurate third-party sources.

Who can build a Business Agent right now? In the initial beta, US ecommerce and online service businesses are eligible. International and offline businesses can claim a profile but cannot yet deploy a Business Agent. OpenAI has not announced a timeline for wider rollout.

Does this compete with our existing customer service tools? Not directly. A Business Agent trained on your policy documents and product information handles top-of-funnel questions. It is not designed to manage escalations, access customer records, or integrate with your CRM without additional custom development. Think of it as a first point of contact, not a full support system.

Will OpenAI start charging for this? The current terms offer free profile claiming and Business Agent creation. OpenAI has not committed to this model, and sponsored placement through ChatGPT Ads is already available. A tiered commercial model as the product matures is a reasonable expectation.

How do we train the Business Agent? The agent draws on documents and information the business provides directly. Your pricing pages, service descriptions, FAQs, and policy documents need to be accurate, complete, and current before you deploy. The quality of the agent's answers depends entirely on the quality of your source material.

## Citable Summary

OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT as a public beta on 10 November 2026. The launch introduced Business Profile

OpenAI Needs to Stop Calling the Retirement of Standard Voice an Upgrade

I’ve been a paying ChatGPT subscriber, and I strongly oppose the decision to retire Standard Voice on December eleventh.

This is not simply about preferring an older voice. This is about losing access to a fundamentally better conversational experience and being forced onto a replacement that, in my experience, is significantly less capable.

Standard Voice allows me to have actual, complex conversations with ChatGPT’s more capable text models. I can discuss complicated technical subjects, explore ideas, work through problems, and maintain a coherent conversation over extended periods.

GPT-Live does not provide an equivalent experience.

Here are my major concerns:

One: A noticeable downgrade in reasoning ability.

GPT-Live routinely struggles with complicated questions and extended technical discussions that Standard Voice handles much better. Its responses often feel shallow, oversimplified, and disconnected from the depth of the conversation.

I use ChatGPT for serious discussions involving artificial intelligence, hardware, software architecture, and other technical subjects. I need the model to actually reason through these discussions, not just produce quick conversational responses.

Two: Interruptions and poor conversational continuity.

Live Voice frequently interrupts, responds before I’ve finished expressing a thought, and struggles to maintain the thread of longer conversations.

Standard Voice allows me to speak naturally, finish my thoughts, and receive a considered response.

That is a significant functional difference, not a minor preference.

Three: The supposed improvements to natural speech are not improvements for everyone.

I actually find Standard Voice more natural and pleasant to listen to.

GPT-Live often sounds artificially expressive, with exaggerated conversational mannerisms and responses that feel scripted or performative.

Trying harder to sound human does not automatically make a system feel more human.

I would rather have a capable model that communicates naturally than a less capable model that performs conversational mannerisms.

Four: Are subscribers being moved to cheaper inference at the expense of quality?

This is a question OpenAI needs to answer transparently.

GPT-Live uses a different architecture from Standard Voice, relying on a voice-focused model with the ability to delegate certain tasks to more capable text models.

That raises a legitimate concern: is OpenAI retiring Standard Voice primarily because GPT-Live is less expensive to operate?

I am not claiming to know OpenAI’s internal costs or motivations. But from a customer’s perspective, it certainly looks like we are being moved away from a more capable experience while continuing to pay the same subscription price.

If cost savings are part of this decision, OpenAI should be transparent about that.

Five: Users are losing choice and functionality.

Why must Standard Voice be removed at all?

If some users prefer GPT-Live, let them use it. But those of us who depend on Standard Voice should be allowed to continue using it.

There is no reason to pretend that every customer has the same needs.

Some people want quick, casual conversations. Others want sustained, technically sophisticated discussions with the strongest available reasoning models.

Both are legitimate uses of ChatGPT.

Six: OpenAI needs to demonstrate actual capability improvements, not just claim them.

I would like to see a direct comparison between Standard Voice and GPT-Live using identical complex questions and extended conversations.

Compare reasoning quality, technical accuracy, context retention, interruptions, and the ability to follow complicated discussions.

If GPT-Live is genuinely an improvement, demonstrate it.

If it cannot match Standard Voice in these areas, stop presenting its replacement as an upgrade.

What I am asking OpenAI to do:

Keep Standard Voice available as an option for paying subscribers.

Preserve the ability to interact through voice with the same capable text models available in normal ChatGPT conversations.

If operating costs are genuinely an obstacle, explain the costs and discuss reasonable alternatives with subscribers rather than removing the functionality outright.

And most importantly, listen to the customers who actually use this feature extensively.

I am paying for access to a capable AI assistant, not simply a voice that sounds conversational.

I do not want a more expressive voice attached to a less capable model. I want the intelligence, reasoning, and conversational depth that made Standard Voice valuable in the first place.

If OpenAI eliminates that experience without providing a genuinely equivalent replacement, I will seriously reconsider continuing my paid subscription.

Please keep Standard Voice.

OpenAI.content:
## post by Mollywhll on Oct 13

I strongly urge OpenAI to reconsider retiring GPT-5.5 while GPT-6 continues to suffer from serious performance and reliability issues.

A large number of users have publicly reported the same recurring problems across Reddit, the OpenAI Developer Community, and other public platforms. These are widespread user complaints, not isolated incidents.

The major issues include:

- Significant performance and intelligence degradation: Declining reasoning ability, comprehension, contextual understanding, and overall task performance.
- Irrelevant responses: Frequently answering questions that users did not ask while failing to address their actual requests.
- Poor editing and revision quality: Producing ineffective revisions, making unauthorized changes, and failing to preserve the original content.
- Failure to follow instructions: Repeatedly ignoring explicit user instructions, restrictions, and corrections.
- Distortion of user intent: Arbitrarily rewriting, reinterpreting, or altering users’ instructions and intended meaning without authorization.
- Failure to verify information: Responding without conducting necessary research or fact-checking.
- Severe hallucinations: Confidently presenting fabricated, inaccurate, or unverified information as facts.

These are fundamental failures in model performance, instruction-following, accuracy, and reliability, not merely differences in user preference.

Despite the large volume of public complaints about GPT-6, OpenAI is proceeding with the retirement of GPT-5.5, a model many users consider significantly more stable and dependable.

Why is OpenAI removing a comparatively stable model while its replacement continues to exhibit serious, widely reported problems?

This decision creates substantial inconvenience, reduces productivity, increases the burden of correcting AI-generated errors, and undermines user trust.

Users should not be forced to accept declining performance simply because a newer model has been released.

I strongly urge OpenAI to:

＊Suspend the retirement of GPT-5.5 until GPT-6’s major performance and reliability issues are resolved.

＊Preserve GPT-5.5 as a legacy option, including limited or paid access if necessary.

＊Seriously investigate and address the widespread user reports of performance degradation, instruction-following failures, poor editing quality, distorted user intent, and severe hallucinations.

Technological progress should improve the user experience, not eliminate a more reliable alternative while forcing users to tolerate a less dependable replacement.

Please take the extensive public feedback seriously and reconsider the retirement of GPT-5.5.

Google.title: Google DeepMind releases benchmark for professional tasks reading blueprints and clinical images
Google.description: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon placed second with 54 percent. ... Claude Fable 5.2 averaged $31.97 per task, about 42,700 won, while Gemini 4 Carbon averaged $6.29, about 8,400 won, about one fifth as much.
Google.content:
# Google DeepMind releases benchmark for professional tasks reading blueprints and clinical images

## AI Summary Google DeepMind has released a new benchmark to assess whether AI agents can perform real professional work, going beyond answering simple questions. The Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark, developed with Artificial Analysis, uses complex visual inputs such as architectural drawings, circuit designs and clinical images and requires agents to produce deliverables like reports and spreadsheets. It spans 200 tasks across 83 job roles, scoring factual accuracy and visual quality.

- Writer Choi Jae-won
- published 2026-11-16 09:11:22
- updated 2026-11-16 09:13:03

Google DeepMind has unveiled a new benchmark to evaluate AI agents' ability to carry out real professional work. It measures capabilities beyond answering simple questions, including analysing complex blueprints and medical images and completing deliverables such as reports and spreadsheets.

On Nov. 14, Taiwan media outlet IT Home reported that Google DeepMind jointly developed the Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark with AI analytics firm Artificial Analysis.

MKA is designed to feed AI systems complex visual information such as architectural drawings, electronic circuit schematics and clinical images, and have them produce real work outputs based on those materials.

There are 200 evaluation tasks, covering 83 job roles across 10 fields including business, construction, engineering, finance, healthcare and science. Each task replicates work that skilled professionals carry out over 3 to 8 hours.

The evaluation does not stop at whether an answer is correct. Each task applies an average of about 70 detailed criteria, weighting 75 percent for factual accuracy and 25 percent for visual completeness.

To ensure a fair comparison, all models were given the same tools and working environment, with up to 250 work opportunities. AI evaluators open the final files and verify the content, formulas and visual composition. Agreement between expert and AI evaluations was 96 percent.

In the results, Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 ranked first with a 57 percent weighted attainment rate on high-difficulty items. Google's Gemini 4 Carbon placed second with 54 percent.

Costs differed widely. Claude Fable 5.2 averaged $31.97 per task, about 42,700 won, while Gemini 4 Carbon averaged $6.29, about 8,400 won, about one fifth as much.

Work efficiency also varied by model. The average number of work iterations needed to complete a task ranged widely from 30 to 130.

Google explained that in professional work, AI agents' competitiveness is expanding beyond simple accuracy rates to include output completeness and cost efficiency. It said the assessment was conducted in a controlled environment, so results may differ from workplace performance in real companies.

About the Author
 Choi Jae-won ittt_0801@d-today.co.kr

# Google DeepMind推出MKA基准：测试AI解析图纸和临床影像并完成工作成果的能力

#### 覆盖10个领域、83个岗位和200项任务，事实准确性权重为75%，视觉完成度占25%

## AI摘要 Google DeepMind与Artificial Analysis联合开发并推出“多模态知识代理”（MKA）基准，要求AI基于建筑图纸、电子电路设计图和临床影像等复杂视觉资料，完成报告、电子表格等可交付成果。该基准共包含200项任务，覆盖10个领域和83个岗位，评分采用细粒度标准，其中事实准确性权重为75%，视觉完成度权重为25%。在已公布结果中，Claude Fable 5.2以57%的综合加权得分位居第一，Gemini 4 Carbon综合加权得分为54%，但后者单项任务成本更低。

- 记者 Choi Jae-won
- 发布时间 2026-11-16 09:11:22

Google DeepMind推出一套面向真实专业岗位的新评测基准，用于衡量AI代理执行复杂工作的能力。与传统评测主要考察问答不同，这套基准要求模型处理复杂图纸和临床影像，并输出报告、电子表格等可直接用于工作的成果。

据台媒IT之家11月14日报道，Google DeepMind与AI分析机构Artificial Analysis联合开发了“多模态知识代理”（MKA）基准。

MKA向AI提供建筑图纸、电子电路设计图、临床影像等复杂视觉资料，并要求其基于相关信息完成最终成果文件，以模拟专业岗位中的实际工作流程。

这套基准共设置200项评测任务，覆盖商业、建筑、工程、金融、医疗、科学等10个领域、83个岗位。每项任务均模拟熟练从业者通常需要3至8小时才能完成的工作。

评测并非只看答案正误。每项任务平均包含约70条细分评分标准，其中事实准确性权重为75%，视觉完成度权重为25%。

为保证结果可比，所有模型使用相同的工具和工作环境，且每个模型最多可进行250次操作。最终文件由AI评审系统打开并核验内容、公式和视觉结构等项目；专家评估与AI评估之间的一致率达到96%。

结果显示，Anthropic的Claude Fable 5.2以57%的综合加权得分排名第一，Google的Gemini 4 Carbon以54%位列第二。

成本差距同样明显。Claude Fable 5.2单项任务平均成本为31.97美元（约合4.27万韩元），Gemini 4 Carbon则为6.29美元（约合8400韩元），约为前者的五分之一。

在效率方面，各模型完成任务所需的平均操作次数介于30次至130次之间，差异较大。

Google表示，在专业工作场景中，AI代理的竞争重点正从单纯的正确率，扩展至成果完成度和成本效率。不过，由于本次评测是在受控环境下进行，其在企业真实业务场景中的实际表现仍可能存在差异。

# DeepSeek 发布全家桶应用 API

2026-11-16 08:37 来源：我的钢铁网(Mysteel) 更多历史数据，上钢联数据

智能摘要 内容由AI生成
11月13日，DeepSeek正式开放全家桶应用API，将App交互功能整合进原有API。V4.1-Flash模型支持联网搜索、深度思考搜索、文件输入（PDF/Office/图片）、阅读链接及模型安全校验等功能。语...展开

据DeepSeek公众号，11月13日，DeepSeek正式开放这套全家桶应用API：在原有API中开启对应参数，即可获得深度思考搜索、文件输入等对话功能；语音及相关底层能力也已开放独立接口（含OCR、ASR、TTS等），支持单独或组合调用。开发者可以在自己的应用中轻松实现复杂的对话功能，甚至1:1复刻出完整的DeepSeekApp。

本次更新将 DeepSeek App 的各项交互功能直接整合进原有 API。开启对应参数后，相关工具调用与上下文拼接均由服务端自动完成。目前，V4.1-Flash 模型（deepseek-flash）已在 Messages、Responses 与 Chat Completions 接口下支持以下能力：

联网搜索：在非思考模式下，打开 deepseek_web_search 工具后，模型可根据提问自动发起网页或图片搜索并附引用作答；

深度思考搜索：在思考模式下，打开 deepseek_web_search 工具后，模型可在多步推理中自主联网搜索与阅读链接；

文件输入：支持上传 PDF、Office、图片等格式的文件，完成纯文本提取或图文混排解析后，拼入对话上下文供模型作答；

阅读链接：将 deepseek_read_url 工具打开后，模型可自动识别用户消息中的链接，抓取网页内容并结合上下文作答；

模型安全：开启安全校验参数后，我们将提供基础风控，审核模型输入输出，命中风险时返回拒答标识。如您对外提供应用服务，请务必开启该参数，并承担内容安全审核、大模型登记、AI 标识等义务。

中国开源模型在全球产业端加速落地

来源：经济参考报作者：荀伟 杨骏 康逸2026-11-16 08:00

字号

日前，2026年网络峰会在葡萄牙首都里斯本举行。本届峰会最鲜明的信号之一，是中国开源人工智能（AI）模型在全球产业端的加速落地。

多位与会专家向记者表示，开源模型正在成为跨越国界与语言的技术“通用语”，让不同发展阶段的国家和地区得以在同一套技术底座上进行创新。其中，来自中国的开源模型正凭借成本可控、部署便捷、技术自主度高等优势，进入越来越多海外企业的生产系统。

网络峰会联合创始人帕迪·科斯格雷夫在开幕式上说，英国金融技术企业雷沃卢特公司已将原先使用的开放人工智能研究中心（OpenAI）与Anthropic公司的编程助手，替换为中国智谱公司的开源GLM系列模型。“雷沃卢特公司的故事，是观察科技未来的一扇窗口——而这个未来，越来越有中国色彩。”

雷沃卢特公司AI基础设施负责人戴维·阿比特博尔向记者介绍，目前GLM模型已成为该公司约2000名工程师的默认编程模型，上线以来，平均编程耗时缩短约60%，AI相关调用成本下降近90%。

法新社在峰会前发表的一篇报道中指出，中国开源模型可以免费下载、支持二次修改，与Anthropic公司、OpenAI的闭源美国模型形成鲜明对比，越来越受欧洲企业青睐。法国电信运营商Orange公司、汽车制造商雷诺以及德国西门子等企业已公开表示使用DeepSeek和通义千问等中国AI模型，作为美国、欧洲本土模型的补充。

“开源AI能够让全球更多国家和企业以较低成本获得先进的AI能力，尤其有助于发展中国家参与新一轮技术变革。”面壁智能首席执行官李大海说，面壁智能已与国内合作伙伴共同参与老挝国家大模型建设，承担模型训练工作。对许多缺乏算力与顶尖人才储备的发展中国家而言，开源模型意味着不必从零训练千亿参数，也能拥有立足本国语言、数据与法规的AI基础设施。

开源模型不仅能惠及发展中国家，对发达国家同样具有吸引力。法新社的报道指出，多数中国模型可以直接部署在欧洲企业自有服务器上，企业认为这样既能保持对数据的掌控，也有利于控制成本。

全球化智库副主任高志凯认为，开源模型具有成本低、技术门槛低等优势，企业可以在开源模型基础上开展二次开发和自主部署，更好地保护数据和商业秘密，减少对外部技术平台的依赖。中国开源模型的发展为欧洲企业提供了新的技术选择，有助于降低数字化转型成本，为中欧在工业AI、智能制造等领域深化合作创造机遇。

美国真实风险投资公司合伙人罗希特·夏尔马说，随着AI技术逐渐成熟，开源技术将在模型开发、推理基础设施等多个环节不断发展，利于AI产业创新。

据主办方介绍，今年中国参会规模创下新高，中国展台被不少欧洲与会者列入“必逛路线”。

Vibe Coding Boom Exposes Corporate Data as AI App Builders Face Security Gaps

스크롤 이동 상태바

# Vibe Coding Boom Exposes Corporate Data as AI App Builders Face Security Gaps

## Grok Build’s default sharing settings and URL design expose sensitive data, including 24 internal SpaceXSI apps

The rise of vibe coding, which enables users to generate code and applications using natural language, has made it easier for non-developers to build business software. However, weak default security designs in AI coding platforms, combined with inadequate corporate data management practices, have led to repeated incidents in which internal information is exposed on the internet.

Recently, data belonging to thousands of users was exposed through Grok Build, a vibe coding agent operated by SpaceXSI, the new name of xAI following its acquisition by SpaceX. The exposed data included proprietary business information and sensitive corporate secrets. According to technology publication Ars Technica, internal data belonging to SpaceXSI itself was also exposed.

Research by security firm Claroc, which first discovered the vulnerability, found that the exposed corporate data included internal business plans, advertising proposals and medical examination results. Some sensitive information originated from 24 applications developed by SpaceXSI itself. Documents found in these applications included a confidential onboarding plan for new enterprise sales employees, a sales territory map covering 594 customer companies, internal system addresses for sales tools and advertising proposals.

Claroc also discovered sensitive data belonging to other Grok Build users, including employees of Fortune 500 companies and defense contractors. A Peruvian construction company had an occupational health dashboard exposing medical examination records for 3,784 workers. At Tesla, a service center performance report containing the real names, productivity figures and bonus payments of 22 mechanics was accessible.

Other exposed information reportedly included personnel rosters for a U.S. Navy ship engineering contractor, a confidential proposal containing a hardware bill of materials (BOM) from a U.S. IT services company, and explosives inventory dashboards and handling procedures at the U.S. facility of a Norwegian-Finnish aerospace and defense group. The companies involved were not identified.

Claroc notified SpaceX of the findings on Nov. 8 but received no response. According to Ars Technica, SpaceXSI removed links to 24 applications created by its own employees and X employees within hours of receiving an email inquiry from the publication. However, Claroc said no separate access restrictions had been implemented for applications created by other users. At the time of Ars Technica’s report, all 24 applications displayed an “App not found” message.

Shared Link Vulnerability Exposes Apps Through Passive DNS

The unintentionally exposed data became accessible through links generated by Grok Build users to share their applications with others. Grok Build’s link-sharing feature is designed to simplify application development and deployment. Users can create internal testing applications within minutes using voice or text prompts and quickly distribute them to authorized users through generated links.

Grok Build generates randomized URLs intended to restrict access to stored data to people who know the exact address. Random word combinations make the URLs difficult for unauthorized parties to guess. This approach is also known as capability-based access control, in which possession of the URL itself grants access to the associated resource.

Each application receives a subdomain consisting of random words, such as “failing-chassis-traders.” Users can modify the subdomain, while the address ends in “grok.me.” Although this makes addresses difficult to guess, the links lose their secrecy if their hostnames are collected by passive DNS services.

The problem is that the randomized string appears in the hostname rather than the URL path. Whenever a user accesses an application, a DNS lookup occurs, potentially allowing the hostname to be collected by passive DNS services. Searching passive DNS databases for grok.me subdomains can therefore reveal large numbers of individual application addresses.

Claroc examined more than 40,000 grok.me subdomains discovered through passive DNS searches and confirmed that 37,571 were online at the time. Of those, 35,578, or 94.7%, allowed access to application interfaces and exposed data without requiring a separate login.

Claroc also reported that a week of testing with a paid account showed the default sharing permission for published applications was “Anyone with the link.” Unless users changed the visibility setting to “invited users” or “only you” during publication, anyone who knew the link could access the application simply by clicking it. Because the URL structure allowed hostnames to be collected through passive DNS, outsiders could discover these applications in large numbers.

According to Claroc, other vibe coding platforms that assign separate hostnames to individual applications, including Lovable, Bolt and Replit, may also allow application addresses to be discovered through passive DNS. However, whether data is actually exposed depends on each application’s visibility settings and implementation of authentication and access controls.

Corporate Vibe Coding Apps Fall Outside Security Governance

Data breaches caused by a combination of design weaknesses in vibe coding platforms and user negligence have become increasingly common.

According to a June report by the Cloud Security Alliance (CSA), The Vibe Coding Governance Gap, social network Moltbook exposed 1.5 million authentication tokens and 35,000 email addresses after embedding a Supabase API key in client-side JavaScript and disabling database row-level security (RLS). Consumer application Cal AI also exposed approximately 3.2 million user records, totaling 14.59GB, because of an unauthenticated Google Firebase backend.

In early May, Israeli security company Red Access examined approximately 380,000 publicly accessible assets associated with vibe coding platforms Lovable, Base44, Replit and Netlify. It found that about 5,000 exposed sensitive corporate and personal information, including medical records, financial data, corporate strategy documents and customer information.

Although it is not an AI coding agent, Meta Muse experienced a similar problem to Grok Build, with approximately 6,800 shared links exposed through passive DNS records. Claroc also discovered this issue, prompting Meta Muse to suspend its conversation-sharing feature on Oct. 20. Because conversation titles appeared in the hostnames of shared links, the links could be reconstructed from DNS records alone. Conversations were accessible without logging in, and some contained sensitive personal and business information.

AI coding platforms allow nonprofessional developers to create applications within minutes and share them through a single link, but security safeguards have taken a back seat, as demonstrated by public-by-default settings, weak access controls and URL designs that make addresses easy to discover and collect. Data breaches recur when users add employee lists, customer information and internal documents without security reviews or checking sharing permissions.

Vibe coding platforms should make private access the default and securely configure authentication and access permissions for individual applications. URL structures should also be improved to prevent easy discovery by outsiders, while authentication mechanisms must not rely solely on obscuring URLs.

Companies must also identify applications created by employees using AI and require those handling customer information and internal documents to undergo the same security reviews as conventional software, including authentication, access controls and data protection. Even in the era of vibe coding, where speed is a competitive advantage, security must be a fundamental requirement considered from the development stage rather than an optional feature added after deployment.

# welaunch.sh· Product launch planner

AI-powered launch distribution plan in minutes

## What is welaunch.sh?

welaunch.sh is a product launch planner.

welaunch.sh is an AI-powered product launch platform designed to help founders, indie hackers, startups, and SaaS creators execute comprehensive product launches across dozens of marketing channels with minimal effort. Instead of spending days or weeks planning a launch strategy, creating content, and manually promoting a product, users simply provide their website URL and the platform generates a complete launch plan powered by a team of specialized AI agents.
The core concept behind welaunch.sh is to automate the entire product launch process. Once a user submits their product URL, a network of nine AI agents analyzes the website, studies the product, identifies the target audience, and creates tailored promotional content for multiple distribution channels. The platform is designed to eliminate the guesswork and repetitive work that often prevents founders from achieving maximum visibility during a launch.
The process begins with the Strategist Agent, which examines the product, understands its value proposition, researches the intended audience, and develops an overall launch strategy. Based on this analysis, the platform generates a detailed launch plan that users can review, edit, and customize before execution. This ensures that the generated content aligns with the product’s positioning, goals, and messaging.
welaunch.sh covers a wide range of promotional channels, including social media platforms, online communities, startup directories, content platforms, and product discovery websites. Supported channels include Reddit, Twitter/X, LinkedIn, Product Hunt, Hacker News, Indie Hackers, Slack communities, Discord servers, Telegram groups, Quora, Facebook Groups, Medium, Dev.to, Hashnode, BetaList, SaaSHub, AlternativeTo, G2, Capterra, and more than 50 startup directories. This broad distribution network allows products to gain exposure across multiple audiences simultaneously.
The platform’s nine AI agents each specialize in a specific aspect of launch marketing. The Community Agent focuses on engaging with communities and discussion platforms. The Social Agent creates social media content optimized for different platforms. The Listing Agent handles directory submissions. The Content Agent develops blog posts and newsletter content. The Product Hunt Agent prepares launch assets such as taglines, descriptions, maker comments, and launch-day checklists. Additional agents focus on SEO content creation, outbound marketing campaigns, and creative growth opportunities.
One of the platform’s unique features is its ability to generate launch-specific content for each channel. Rather than reusing the same message everywhere, the AI adapts the copy, tone, and format to match the expectations and culture of each platform. This helps founders avoid generic promotion and create more effective outreach campaigns.
welaunch.sh also aims to simplify the launch process by consolidating all launch activities into a single workflow. Users can review the generated content, enable or disable specific channels, make adjustments, and then launch their campaign from one central dashboard. According to the platform, the entire launch plan can be generated in approximately 30 seconds.
With a pay-per-launch pricing model, no subscriptions, and access to all nine AI agents, welaunch.sh positions itself as a cost-effective solution for startups and entrepreneurs seeking wider product visibility. By combining AI-driven strategy, content creation, directory submissions, community engagement, social media promotion, SEO preparation, and outbound marketing, the platform serves as a complete launch assistant designed to help products reach a larger audience and maximize launch-day impact.

# 软银与 Grab 签约在马来西亚建人工智能设施，计划首期出资 18.5 亿美元

11 月 9 日，软银集团与 Grab 签署联合开发协议，计划在砂拉越和马来半岛建设人工智能设施；砂拉越项目由砂拉越州石油公司 PETROS 一同参与。计划首期出资 18.5 亿美元，资金分期到位。

数据速览

- 计划首期启动资金
- 18.5 亿美元
- 砂拉越项目计划额
- 10 亿美元
- 半岛项目计划额
- 8.5 亿美元
- 长期算力容量目标
- 5 吉瓦以上

软银集团与东南亚出行和外卖平台 Grab 于 2026 年 11 月 9 日签署联合开发协议，计划在马来西亚的砂拉越和马来半岛建设人工智能基础设施。砂拉越位于婆罗洲北部，与马来半岛相对；砂拉越项目由该州国有石油公司 PETROS 一同参与。计划首期启动资金合计 18.5 亿美元，将在达到约定建设节点和客户合同节点、并满足交割条件后分批到位。

砂拉越项目按计划出资 10 亿美元，其中软银集团出 8 亿美元，Grab 与 PETROS 各出 1 亿美元。马来半岛项目按计划出资 8.5 亿美元，其中 Grab 出 6.5 亿美元，软银集团出 2 亿美元。协议中的开发与出资义务具有约束力，合资公司的设立和各方出资条款仍待最终协议。

砂拉越项目由软银集团主导并保持控股。Grab 若提高持股，软银集团的股权比例会下降，但仍是控股股东。半岛项目由 Grab 以创始股东身份牵头，规模扩大时再引入长期战略投资者。半岛项目的后续建设资金预计由项目公司对外筹集，包括第三方股权和无追索融资；后者指债权人原则上只能向项目资产求偿。

Grab 联合创始人、董事长兼首席执行官陈炳耀（Anthony Tan）预计将统筹两个项目，并任命专职团队负责日常运营；他本人继续领导 Grab。Grab 董事会已审议并同意他参与这两个项目。软银集团还原则上同意，旗下一家主体将直接持有的 Grab 股份锁定五年，有常规例外。

此次协议接续三方 2026 年 10 月 8 日在古晋签署的框架协议。公司称，两地长期目标是 5 吉瓦（1 吉瓦等于 100 万千瓦）以上的算力容量，全面投运后有望成为亚洲规模最大的同类设施之一。设施将按马来西亚可再生能源使用指引运营，设计上减少用水、降低对当地电网的依赖。PETROS 将依托砂拉越天然气路线图和古晋低碳枢纽，提供能源和园区方面的经验；各方还会寻找更多投资人和超大规模云厂商客户。

马来西亚近期还有两项大型人工智能算力投资。谷歌于 2026 年 11 月 4 日宣布，2027 年至 2028 年在马来西亚投入 150 亿美元；新园区选在雪兰莪和森美兰。数据中心公司 Firmus 已于 2026 年 9 月 8 日与 OpenAI 签约。根据协议，OpenAI 将采购 Firmus 在马来西亚两座人工智能数据中心的专用算力，成为其锚定客户（即带动项目建设的主力客户）。
